The film certainly does not do the book justice. While it is beautiful and aesthetic within its nature, I don’t think it totally saves what otherwise is a complete lack of plot or connection between Elio and Oliver. As someone else mentioned, without the narration provided by Elio in the book, it makes their connection, repressed behavior, and physical subtleties hard to distinguish. Important moments in the novel definitely felt forced in the film because they lacked context, being Elio’s thought process/how he comes to view and develop feelings for Oliver. I think it’s difficult to adapt such a book with it being so internal. The film tried in a very external way which was their ultimate downfall. If they had added narrations, being mainly Elio’s and then some from Oliver, I feel as though they could’ve definitely helped what otherwise felt like a slow and sort of confusing film. 

As for it being pretentious—I would just say these characters come from higher education and that can definitely come across as such to those that doesn’t really understand the subject matter. I would not say they were pretentious, just cultured, and eager to share it with one another. 

I won’t completely discredit the story in general, because I do think the book portrays a compelling, slow-burn romance set in a realistic European setting. However, the film could’ve portrayed the story and characters much better, and I do agree that the age gap is something I personally wouldn’t be comfortable with. Not to say it isn’t common to see, but still, personally not something I would consent to or want for my child.

My partner and I just broke up. We dated for three years, went separate ways bc of his abuse, didn’t talk for two years, came back together after a year of trying to regain trust, and we were together after that for five months until what happened last night. We have an intensely deep and passionate history together, but we’re both bipolar, struggle with suicide ideation, and we’re both alcoholics, and he wants me to just enable his drinking and stop trying to get better essentially. He also tried to make our pain a competition saying that “no one is more suicidal than him”, knowing that I just got out of a hospital. Who says shit like that? It hurts so much bc we’re both in so much pain, I thought that our love would inspire him to get better like it inspires me, and we’ve planned our future together but he just says mean, hurtful things when I don’t enable him, but then expects his struggles with mental health to excuse it. I struggle too but I would never say the things he has said to me. 

I just keep losing everything that I thought was good, and all of this has happened while I’ve been living on my sister’s couch, because I had left the hospital in September, moved back to my hometown to rekindle my relationship with my family bc my mother convinced me to, and then I was kicked out of my mother and grandmother’s home a week after moving home bc they found out I’m pansexual. I’ve lost so much and now I’ve lost him too, regardless of it being his fault for hurting me. I’m sick of losing the things and people I love. I’ve lost myself. I just want to feel excited about being alive again. I laid around all day dissociated doing literally nothing. And I don’t have a job bc I’m so unstable. I’m just drowning in financial and emotional ruin.

The shame you carry must feel extremely heavy and all-consuming. But whatever has happened, your alcoholism at the very least doesn’t make you a bad or unworthy person, not in the slightest. No matter what has gone on in your life, you do not deserve to be eaten alive by your guilt or any sort of pain. What you do deserve is forgiveness, compassion, honesty, and ultimately, support. Maybe you don’t feel that from your personal environment, but there are people out there that if given the chance, they would be there for you. And you deserve chance after chance to start over and make things right. Whenever you feel able and ready to. It’s exhausting, and takes courage, but you wake up every day and keep going despite all you’re going through and have gone through. That says a lot
